titel: Base rule set for a new project
kurz: A new project does not have to start with empty rules: the AMW ships a base rule set – rules that have proven themselves in working with agents, each with its reason. When creating the project you choose what should apply.
brauchst: The “New project” assistant (project selector › + New project) or the command `amw einrichten`.
An idea of who leads the project: if the lead works as a chat, the rhythm rule is added.

schritte.text: In the assistant, “Rule set” shows “Base rule set (default)”. Other options: copy the working rules of an existing project, or start without rules.
Open “… rules chosen – view and adjust”. The rules come in three groups (work and evidence, decisions and knowledge, safety and operation), plus a few optional ones.
No tick means: does not apply in this project. You can change the wording in the field. Below every rule you find its reason – or the experience it comes from.
Together with the project, the chosen rules are created as working rules, a decision as their source, the definition of done in the charter, and the first version 0.1.0.
Like any rule: the lead records a decision and changes the rule with it (`amw beschluss neu`, then `amw regel` with the number of the decision).

werte: “Base rule set” is preselected; “copy of …” takes the working rules of another project
all base rules are ticked, the optional ones are not
default from the template – change it if your project does it differently
fehler: The base rule set can only be taken over when the project is created. Into an existing project, single rules come through a decision.
Either pick “none” or tick at least one rule.
The rule should read differently from the template
Change the wording; the rule stays recognisable as a base rule and carries the note “adjusted”.
danach: Under Knowledge › Rules the base rules form a group of their own, with their number from the template (G1 …) and the reason.
Every session gets the number of rules, and changed rules verbatim, in its start information; `amw regeln` shows all of them.
What your project needs specifically (who reviews, who merges, which branches) is added by the lead as rules of its own.
fragen: What is the difference between “Why” and “Experience”?
“Experience” only appears where an occasion is on record. All other rules have a “Why” – the reason given by the rule itself. Invented incidents appear nowhere.
Does a new edition of the template change my rules?
No. Your rules are a copy of their own. A new edition overwrites nothing.
Why does the project start at version 0.1.0?
The scheme is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. 1.0.0 is the first stable, usable release; until then 0.x counts.
And a project that already exists?

Knowledge › Rules › “Comparison with the base rule set” puts each base rule next to your rules: adopted, probably covered by an own rule (with a pointer) or missing. It is a proposal only – your rules stay as they are. “Adopt” adds a missing base rule with the next free number; a decision records the source. At the PC: `amw regelwerk abgleich --ablegen` files the comparison as a document and sends it to the lead; `amw regelwerk uebernehmen G7` adopts one rule.
